question.:question/problem:
Determine the value of $k$ for which the following system of linear equations is inconsistent:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-3y &=2 \\ -3x+ky &=2\end{aligned}\right.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & 2 \\ -3 & k & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & 2 \\ -3 & k & 2\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & k-9 & 8\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-3y &=2 \\ (k-9)y &=8.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The system is inconsistent if it has no solutions. For the system to have no solutions, one of the equations above must be false.

If $k=9,$ then the second equation is $0=8,$ which is false, and the system will have no solution.

Therefore, our system is inconsistent when $k=9.$

$$
